cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the saints in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He just said God does not show favoritism (Romans 2:11). Now he talks straight to you, if you call yourself a Jew.

cards.question: Paul goes on: if you rely on something and boast in God. What does Paul say you rely on?

cards.text: Paul's list of ifs keeps going: if you know God's will and approve of what is superior, because the law instructs you. If you're convinced you're a guide for the blind…

cards.question: In Paul's list, the one who calls himself a Jew is also convinced he's a light for those in darkness.

cards.text: Paul adds: if you're convinced you're an instructor of the foolish and a teacher of infants, because in the law you have the embodiment of knowledge and truth. Me? I've only ever had one title, Papa, and I had to ask an angel if I could keep it.

cards.question: After that whole list, Paul turns his questions on the one who instructs others. What does Paul ask him?

answers.text: Do you not learn from others
Do you not test your students

cards.question: Paul asks the one who preaches against stealing whether he steals.
Paul asks the one who abhors idols whether he robs temples. Just before that, he asks the one who forbids another sin if he commits it. Which sin?
Paul asks the one who boasts in the law: by breaking the law, do you ___ God?

cards.text: Paul's questions are like me hanging a big NO TASTING THE DOUGH sign while there's dough all over my mustache. Then Paul quotes Scripture (Isaiah 52:5) about what this does to God's name.

cards.question: Paul quotes Scripture to the one who boasts in the law: God's name is blasphemed because of you. Among whom is it blasphemed?

cards.text: Next Paul brings up circumcision, the sign of the covenant God gave Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 17:10-11). Hold onto your apron, friend, because Paul's about to say what that sign is really worth.

cards.question: Paul says circumcision has value on one condition. What is it?
Paul says if you break the law, your circumcision still counts as circumcision.

cards.text: Now Paul flips the whole thing over. Picture a man who isn't circumcised, but he keeps the requirements of the law.

cards.question: Paul asks whether the uncircumcised man who keeps the requirements of the law will be regarded as circumcised.
Paul says the physically uncircumcised man who keeps the law will ___ the lawbreaker who has the written code and circumcision.

cards.text: Then Paul says a man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, and circumcision isn't only outward and physical. So what counts, friend?

cards.question: Paul says a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the ___, not by the written code.
Paul says a man who is a Jew inwardly gets his praise from other people.
